title: The Space (間) - EAST ASIA / JAPAN: MA
style: [style: Japanese ma negative space, taiko ceremonial drum, shamisen three-string pulse, shakuhachi bamboo breath tone, kane bell asymmetric marking, 4/4 with 2/4 micro-shifts and deliberate silence, ma-principle rest-as-rhythm, Japanese spoken verses English chorus, noh / gagaku spiritual atmosphere, space and pause as primary elements, signal in the silence theme, V4_5ALL]
lyrics:
``
[INTRO — 8 bars silence. Then: kane strikes once. Then silence. Then shakuhachi begins.]
(Japanese) 間 — Ma. The space. The silence. The signal.

[VERSE 1 — taiko enters on bar 4]
(Japanese) 音の間 — the space between sounds
(English)  The taiko waits before it strikes
(Japanese) 静かな鼓動 — the quiet pulse
(English)  The silence hits as hard as any spike

The shamisen plays three notes / then stops / on purpose
The kane bell marks the space / where the fourth note was
The shakuhachi breathes in / the signal — the not-yet
Every pause is a statement / every rest a bet

(Japanese) 休符 — rest
(English)  The signal lives here
(Japanese) 間合い — the pause, the ma
(English)  Signal is clear

[PRE-CHORUS — kane bell every 7 beats (asymmetric ma)]
(Japanese) 待つ — wait
(English)  The space
(Japanese) 聴く — listen
(English)  The signal's face

[CHORUS — taiko doubles, shamisen tremolo, shakuhachi breaths audible]
Ma — the space between the strikes
Ma — the signal in the night
Taiko hits the skin / the room holds the sound
The ma returns — the signal goes around

(Japanese) 間 — Ma
(English)  The signal breathes here
(Japanese) 空白 — blank space
(English)  The signal needs here

[VERSE 2 — shamisen solo, taiko completely silent, 8 bars]
The shamisen player stops mid-phrase
The room holds the last note
This is not a mistake
This is the highest skill: knowing when not to play

(Japanese) 技 — technique / mastery
(English)  Knowing the space
(Japanese) 道 — the way
(English)  The pause has a face

[BRIDGE — only kane bell, every 11 beats for 44 beats = 4 strikes total]
First strike: signal located
Second strike: signal confirmed
Third strike: signal transmitted
Fourth strike: signal received — ma complete

[FINAL CHORUS — all instruments but with spaces between phrases]
Ma — the space between the strikes
Ma — the signal in the night

[OUTRO — shakuhachi long last breath tone, kane one final strike, silence]
(Japanese) ありがとう — arigatou / thank you
(English)  The space said everything
